newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland sees A$7.6 mln 96/97 surplus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland sees A$7.6 mln 96/97 surplus.

text.p: The Australian state of Queensland has projected an underlying budget surplus of A$7.6 million in the 1996/97 fiscal year (July/June), after posting a A$180.4 million deficit in 1995/96, Treasurer Joan Sheldon said. In headline terms, the government has forecast a 1996/97 surplus of A$247 million, down from the A$1.354 billion surplus of 1995/96.
The State Government's net financing requirement was forecast at negative A$201 million, compared with negative $289 million in 1995/96 .
The headline surplus and borrowing requirement are calculated under the Government Financial Statistics (GFS) methodology.

The GFS surplus includes contributions from investments, repayments of debt, changes in cash balances and other outlays made for the purpose of acquiring financial assets and/or reducing financial liabilities.
Sheldon said she was presenting a "back to basics" budget when announcing it to the parliament.
"From the very start, the Coalition Government promised a balanced budget with no deficit, and this is what we have delivered," Sheldon said.
Sheldon said the previous government had generated a small surplus of A$5.4 million for 1995/96, but this had been propped up by one-off measures worth about A$186 million.
"The consequences are that an underlying deficit of A$180.4 million in 1995/96 must be carried forward as an additional burden to taxpayers in 1996/97."
On a no policy-change basis this would increase to a deficit of A$240 million in 1996/97, she said.
Combined with Health Department cost overruns, cuts from the Commonwealth of A$250 million, had created a budgetary hole of more than A$500 million, Sheldon said.

The government would offset these through savings of A$500 million against the forward estimates for 1996/97 from recurrent expenditure, and A$140 million of election committments from the previous Labor administration that were unfunded will not proceed, Sheldon said.
"The result of our hard wark is that we have restored the operating position of the government to balance," Sheldon said.
